name: Weather Conditions
description: Rain, snow, or extreme heat can significantly impact robot movement speed and stability, leading to longer travel times.

name: Terrain Type
description: Rough terrain like slopes or uneven ground will increase travel times compared to smooth surfaces.

name: Lighting Conditions
description: Shadows, glare, or low light can affect camera image quality and potentially lead to slower navigation.

name: Vegetation Density & Type
description: Dense vegetation can obstruct the robot's line of sight, causing delays and increased distance travelled.

name: Soil Composition
description: The soil type can affect the robot's stability and traction, influencing travel time.

name: Obstacle Density
description: The presence of obstacles like rocks, weeds, or downed trees will force the robot to take detours and slow down.

name: Path Width & Length
description: Narrower paths or longer segments will result in more movement and more time spent navigating.

name: Robot Speed/Agility
description: The robot's inherent speed and maneuverability influences its ability to efficiently cover longer distances.

name: GPS Signal Strength
description: Weak GPS signals could lead to inaccurate positioning and route deviations, impacting navigation speed.

name: Sensor Calibration
description: Inaccurate sensor readings can cause errors that impact the robot's path.

name: Robot Maintenance
description: Mechanical issues could cause the robot to move erratically, slowing it down.

name: Path Markings
description: The quality and clarity of path markings could be a factor that influences the robot's path.

name: Robot Orientation
description: Incorrect orientation can cause the robot to follow suboptimal paths or take unexpected turns.

name: Dynamic Field Conditions (e.g., Wind)
description: Strong wind can significantly alter the robot's path, potentially increasing travel times.
